question: Whales and sturgeon off England's coast still belong to the Crown, by a statute of the 1320s. Which of these English laws are real?
answer: Old laws last when keeping them costs nobody anything. De Prerogativa Regis, usually dated to about 1324, makes whales and sturgeon royal fish, and nobody has troubled to repeal it; strandings still go to the Receiver of Wreck. The funny old laws that circulate are mostly invented, so nobody can cite them.
move: Old rules survive when keeping them costs nobody anything.

items.note: Whales and sturgeon caught off the coast go to the Crown.
items.verdict: From a statute of about 1324, never repealed.

items.note: In Chester you may shoot a Welshman with a longbow.
items.verdict: No such law has ever been traced, in Chester or anywhere else.

items.note: 1267: limits on seizing a debtor's goods.
items.verdict: A few chapters still in force, 750 years on.

items.note: A pregnant woman may relieve herself in one.
items.verdict: No law, old or new, says so.

items.note: Coming to Parliament in armour is banned.
items.verdict: A statute of 1313, still in force.

items.note: Eating them on Christmas Day is illegal.
items.verdict: Puritan bans on Christmas lapsed in 1660.
An offence under the Salmon Act 1986, aimed at poached fish.
